en: Py allows you to manage your sessions. It
gives you commands like fork and clone,
which allow you, for example, to branch a
session into a new file or to copy the
current branch. And these 2 are actually
almost the same. The only difference is
which starting point is used for branching
out. But the idea is essentially that you
copy your session, that you copy the session
file effectively, and that you therefore
duplicate a session. And you got 2 copies of
the session you can now work on, which each
has the context at which point you copied
it, but then the new context of where you
continue a session.
And then there also is another command,
/tree, which is a bit more powerful, which
allows you to branch out inside of a
session. So inside of one and the same
session file and follow down different paths
and merge them together and so on. But
again, we'll see that in action later. For
now, let's see fork and clone in action
because these are the easier ones. And
whilst I typically don't use them that
often, they can also be useful.
